newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cetelem rise on catch-up, buy-out talk.
newsitem.headline: Cetelem rise on catch-up, buy-out talk.

text.p: Shares in French consumer credit house Cetelem rose sharply on Friday, driven by hopes of a buy-out offer from Paribas or parent Cie Bancaire and helped by catch-up too, market sources said.
Cetelem gained 5.65 percent to 1,215 francs on 17,970 shares at 1253 GMT.

The shares broke through major resistance at the opening at 1,160 francs and is well placed to hit 1,400, based on chart performance, said one operator. The shares were also seen to be correcting after having lagged recently.
Takeover talks also helped the share run up.
Cetelem declined to comment in the buy-out talk.
One market operator said Cetelem had turned out good results in a difficult economic climate weak consumption, so it had everything to gain from lower interest rates and a recovery.
"Cetelem is a "great growth stock and extremely well managed," said one fund manager.
The company posted first half net attributable profit up 14 percent at 590 million francs.
